The seat belongs to one bonded warehouse receipt. A licensed elevator weighs the load, prints a serial ticket and files the receipt; the node reads that registry, rejects serials seen before, and rechecks bin capacity yearly. Grain hauled down a canyon on the tide, milled into pearl rice, does not change the paper, and one bin issues one ticket however many buyers hold shares.

Five thousand bushels at 4.20 is 21,000 dollars, storage 1,750 a year, so fifty seats need 250,000 weighed bushels, near 1.1 million dollars. One silo holds one harvest, whatever names get painted on the door.
